questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Quantisation of electric charge means that the charge on any body is
options: any real number multiple of e
questions.explanation: Charge exists only in whole-number multiples of the elementary charge e, so q = ne.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Which of the following is a correct unit of electric field?
questions.explanation: Electric field is force per unit charge (N/C), which is equivalent to V/m.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Two point charges of 2 microcoulomb and 3 microcoulomb are 0.3 m apart in air. The force between them is (k = 9 × 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Capacitors of 2 microfarad and 4 microfarad are connected in parallel. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: In parallel the capacitances add: 2 + 4 = 6 microfarad.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: A point charge q is placed at the centre of a cube. The electric flux through one face of the cube is
questions.explanation: The total flux q/epsilon_0 is shared equally among the six identical faces.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Charges of +2 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb are 0.1 m apart. The electrostatic potential energy of this pair is (k = 9 × 10^9 N m^2 C^-2)
questions.explanation: U = k q1 q2 / r = 9 × 10^9 × (-4 × 10^-12)/0.1 = -0.36 J; the negative sign shows the charges attract.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Why can two electric field lines never cross each other?
questions.answer: The tangent to a field line at a point gives the direction of the electric field there. If two lines crossed, the field at the crossing point would have two directions at once, which is impossible, so field lines never intersect.
keyPoints: Crossing would mean two directions at one point
Field has a unique direction at every point
questions.explanation: The same logic applies to lines of force in any vector field.

questions.topic: Electrostatics: Charges, Fields, Potential and Capacitors
questions.q: Why is it relatively safe to stay inside a closed metal car during a lightning storm?
questions.answer: The metal body acts as a conducting shell. The charge from lightning spreads over the outer surface and the electric field inside a hollow conductor is zero, so the passengers inside are shielded from the discharge.
keyPoints: Car body acts as a hollow conductor
Charge stays on the outer surface
questions.explanation: This principle is also used in Faraday cages.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Which material is used as the core of an electromagnet?
questions.explanation: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, which suits electromagnets.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: Two resistors of 3 ohm and 5 ohm are connected in series. Their equivalent resistance is
questions.explanation: In series the resistances add: 3 + 5 = 8 ohm.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A steady current of 0.5 A flows in a wire for 10 minutes. The charge that passes through the wire is

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: An electron moves at 2 × 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. The magnetic force on it is (e = 1.6 × 10^-19 C)

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced with P = 10 ohm, Q = 20 ohm and R = 30 ohm, where P/Q = R/S. The value of S is

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: When the temperature of a semiconductor is raised, its resistance
questions.explanation: More charge carriers are released at higher temperature, so the resistance of a semiconductor falls, unlike that of a metal.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: State the Biot-Savart law.
questions.answer: The magnetic field dB produced at a point by a small current element I dl is directly proportional to the current, the length of the element and the sine of the angle between dl and the line to the point, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance, dB = (mu_0/4 pi) I dl sin(theta)/r^2.
keyPoints: dB proportional to I dl sin(theta)
questions.explanation: It is used to find the field of loops and other current distributions.

questions.topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
questions.q: A current loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field. Why does it rotate but not move as a whole?
questions.answer: The forces on opposite sides of the loop are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero and there is no translation. These forces are not along the same line, so they form a couple that exerts a torque tau = m B sin(theta) and rotates the loop.
questions.explanation: This is the principle of the moving-coil galvanometer and the electric motor.

questions.q: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday (and independently Joseph Henry) discovered electromagnetic induction in the 1830s.

questions.q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is
questions.explanation: Flux = B × A, and one weber equals one tesla metre squared.

questions.q: A loop of area 0.2 m^2 is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T with the field making an angle of 60 degrees with the normal to the loop. The magnetic flux is
questions.explanation: Flux = B A cos(60 degrees) = 0.5 × 0.2 × 0.5 = 0.05 Wb.

questions.q: An alternating current has a peak value of 5 A. Its rms value is about
An ideal step-up transformer has a turns ratio of 1 : 10. If the primary current is 10 A, the secondary current is
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer V_p I_p = V_s I_s; the voltage is raised 10 times, so the current falls to one tenth, 1 A.

questions.q: A metal rod 0.5 m long moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T, with its length perpendicular to both. The motional emf across its ends is
Distinguish between self-induction and mutual induction.
questions.answer: In self-induction a changing current in a coil induces an emf in the same coil. In mutual induction a changing current in one coil induces an emf in a neighbouring coil. The emf is characterised by the self-inductance L or the mutual inductance M, both measured in henry.
questions.explanation: Transformers use mutual induction; chokes use self-induction.

questions.q: A bulb connected in series with a coil with iron core glows dimly when connected to an AC source, but brightly when connected to a DC source of the same voltage. Explain.
questions.answer: With AC the inductor offers reactance X_L = 2 pi f L in addition to resistance, so the impedance is high and the current is small. With DC there is no change in current once steady, so there is no back emf and only the small resistance of the coil limits the current.
questions.explanation: An inductor passes DC easily but opposes AC, and more so at higher frequency.

questions.q: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour is deviated the most?
questions.explanation: Violet has the highest refractive index in glass and therefore bends the most.

questions.q: The focal length of a plane mirror is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror is a surface of infinite radius of curvature, so f = infinity.

questions.q: An object is placed 30 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 30 cm. The image is formed at
options: 15 cm in front of the mirror
60 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/30 + 1/30 = 1/15, so v = +15 cm, a virtual image behind the mirror.

questions.q: Two thin lenses of powers +10 D and -2 D are placed in contact. The focal length of the combination is
questions.explanation: Total power = 10 - 2 = 8 D, so f = 1/8 m = 12.5 cm.

questions.q: A prism of angle 60 degrees has refractive index root 2. The angle of minimum deviation is
questions.explanation: n = sin((A + D)/2)/sin(A/2) gives sin((A + D)/2) = root 2 × 0.5 = 0.707, so (A + D)/2 = 45 degrees and D = 30 degrees.

questions.q: Two ordinary bulbs shone on a screen do not produce a stable interference pattern because
options: the bulbs have different powers only
the light from them is not coherent
questions.explanation: Independent sources emit with rapidly and randomly changing phase differences, so the pattern keeps shifting and averages out.

questions.q: Distinguish between a real image and a virtual image.
questions.answer: A real image is formed when light rays actually meet at a point; it can be obtained on a screen and is inverted for a single mirror or lens. A virtual image is formed when rays only appear to diverge from a point; it cannot be taken on a screen and is erect.
keyPoints: Real: rays actually meet, can be projected
Virtual: rays appear to come from a point, cannot be projected
Real is usually inverted, virtual erect
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms virtual images.

questions.q: Why is blue light preferred to red light when a microscope is used to see very fine detail?
questions.answer: The limit of resolution is proportional to the wavelength of light used. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red, so it can resolve objects that are closer together and gives a sharper view of fine detail.
keyPoints: Resolution limit is proportional to wavelength
Blue wavelength is shorter than red
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes use even smaller de Broglie wavelengths.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: The SI unit of radioactivity is
questions.explanation: One becquerel is one decay per second.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Which radiation from radioactive substances has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays are high-energy photons with no charge and penetrate matter the most.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: In beta-minus decay of a nucleus, the atomic number
options: increases by 1 and the mass number is unchanged
decreases by 1 and the mass number is unchanged
decreases by 2 and the mass number decreases by 4
is unchanged and the mass number increases by 1
questions.explanation: A neutron changes into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino, so Z rises by 1 and A stays the same.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Photoelectrons from a surface have a maximum kinetic energy of 3 eV. The stopping potential is
questions.explanation: eV_0 = K_max, so V_0 = 3 V.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Using E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV, the energy of the photon emitted in the transition n = 3 to n = 2 in hydrogen is about

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Nuclear density is nearly the same for all nuclei because
options: nuclear volume is proportional to the mass number
nuclear radius is independent of mass number
questions.explanation: R is proportional to A^(1/3), so volume is proportional to A, and mass is also proportional to A, making density constant.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: What is radioactivity?
questions.answer: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation, such as alpha particles, beta particles or gamma rays, from the nuclei of unstable atoms as they change into more stable nuclei.
keyPoints: Emission of alpha, beta or gamma radiation
questions.explanation: It was discovered by Henri Becquerel.

questions.topic: Dual Nature of Radiation, Atoms and Nuclei
questions.q: Compare nuclear fission and nuclear fusion in two points.
questions.answer: In fission a heavy nucleus such as uranium-235 splits into two lighter nuclei after absorbing a neutron, releasing energy and more neutrons. In fusion two light nuclei such as hydrogen isotopes combine to form a heavier nucleus and release energy, but it needs a very high temperature to overcome the Coulomb repulsion.
questions.explanation: Fusion is the source of the Sun's energy.

questions.q: Which of the following solutions does not conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a non-electrolyte and does not produce ions in solution.

questions.q: The value of one faraday is approximately
questions.explanation: One faraday is the charge of one mole of electrons, about 96 500 C.

questions.q: 10 g of sodium chloride is dissolved in 90 g of water. The mass percentage of NaCl in the solution is
The vapour pressure of pure liquid A is 100 mm Hg. In an ideal solution where the mole fraction of A is 0.6, the partial vapour pressure of A is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law p_A = x_A p_A^0 = 0.6 × 100 = 60 mm Hg.

questions.q: The osmotic pressure of a 0.01 M solution of a non-electrolyte at 300 K is (R = 0.0821 L atm mol^-1 K^-1)
In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride with inert electrodes, the gas liberated at the cathode is
questions.explanation: Water is reduced more easily than Na+, so H2 forms at the cathode, Cl2 at the anode and NaOH is left in solution.

questions.q: What are azeotropes?
questions.answer: Azeotropes are liquid mixtures that boil at a constant temperature and distil over with the same composition as the liquid, so they cannot be separated by simple fractional distillation. Ethanol-water mixture at about 95 per cent ethanol is an example.
keyPoints: Vapour has same composition as liquid
Cannot be separated by fractional distillation
questions.explanation: They form from non-ideal solutions showing large deviations from Raoult's law.

questions.q: Why does zinc-coated (galvanised) iron resist rusting even when the zinc coating is scratched?
questions.answer: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so in the presence of moisture it is oxidised in preference to iron and acts as a sacrificial anode. The exposed iron acts as the cathode and is protected from corrosion until the zinc is used up.
keyPoints: Zinc is more reactive than iron
questions.explanation: Tin coating, in contrast, only protects while the surface is intact.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The unit of the rate of a chemical reaction is
questions.explanation: Rate is the change in concentration per unit time.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Which transition metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury has a melting point of about -39 degrees C because of its filled d subshell and weak metallic bonding.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: A first-order reaction has k = 0.0231 min^-1. The half-life is

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: The spin-only magnetic moment of an ion with three unpaired electrons is about
questions.explanation: mu = root(n(n + 2)) = root 15, which is about 3.87 BM.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: In an Arrhenius plot of ln k against 1/T, the slope of the straight line is
questions.explanation: ln k = ln A - Ea/(RT), so the slope is -Ea/R.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Mn2+ is very difficult to oxidise to Mn3+ mainly because
options: Mn2+ has a half-filled 3d5 configuration which is particularly stable
Mn2+ has a completely filled 3d subshell
Mn3+ is smaller than a proton
questions.explanation: The d5 configuration of Mn2+ has extra stability due to exchange energy, whereas Fe2+ (d6) oxidises easily to the d5 Fe3+ ion.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: What is a pseudo first-order reaction? Give an example.
questions.answer: It is a reaction that is actually of higher order but behaves as first order because one reactant is present in such large excess that its concentration is practically constant. Hydrolysis of ethyl ethanoate in excess water or the inversion of cane sugar are examples.
keyPoints: Higher order reaction behaving as first order
Example: hydrolysis of ester or inversion of sucrose
questions.explanation: The constant concentration of water is absorbed into the rate constant.

questions.topic: Chemical Kinetics and the d- and f-Block Elements
questions.q: Write the balanced ionic equation for the oxidation of ferrous ions by permanganate in acidic medium.
questions.answer: 5Fe2+ + MnO4- + 8H+ gives 5Fe3+ + Mn2+ + 4H2O. Each Fe2+ loses one electron and each permanganate ion accepts five electrons.
questions.explanation: The decolourisation of the purple permanganate marks the end point of the titration.

questions.q: Which of the following is a neutral ligand?
questions.explanation: Water is an uncharged molecule that donates a lone pair of electrons through oxygen.

questions.q: The anticancer drug cisplatin is a coordination complex of
questions.explanation: Cisplatin is cis-[Pt(NH3)2Cl2].

questions.q: How many ions are produced per formula unit when [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissolves in water?
questions.explanation: It gives one [Co(NH3)6]3+ ion and three Cl- ions, four ions in all.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex ion [Cu(NH3)4]2+ is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named first (tetraammine) followed by the metal with its oxidation state, copper(II) here.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in an octahedral high-spin d4 complex?
questions.explanation: In a weak field the electrons occupy t2g^3 eg^1 with all four unpaired, while a strong field gives t2g^4 with two unpaired.

questions.q: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br and [Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 are ionisation isomers. Which statement is correct?
options: [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br gives a pale-yellow precipitate with silver nitrate
[Co(NH3)5Br]SO4 gives a pale-yellow precipitate with silver nitrate
both give a precipitate with barium chloride
questions.explanation: In [Co(NH3)5SO4]Br the bromide ion is outside the coordination sphere and precipitates as AgBr, while in the other isomer bromide is bound and sulphate is free.

questions.q: Define coordination number and coordination sphere with an example.
questions.answer: The coordination number is the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to the central metal ion. The coordination sphere is the central metal with the ligands attached to it, written in square brackets. In [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 the coordination number is 6 and the sphere is [Co(NH3)6]3+.
keyPoints: Number of donor atoms bonded to the metal
Coordination sphere is within square brackets
Example with Co and six NH3
questions.explanation: Counter ions outside the brackets are not part of the sphere.

questions.q: Why are chelate complexes more stable than comparable complexes with monodentate ligands?
questions.answer: A polydentate ligand forms ring structures with the metal and, when it replaces several monodentate ligands, the number of free particles in solution increases. This raises the entropy and makes the complex more stable, which is called the chelate effect.
questions.explanation: For example [Ni(en)3]2+ is more stable than [Ni(NH3)6]2+.

questions.q: The compound C6H5OH is called
questions.explanation: A hydroxyl group attached directly to a benzene ring gives phenol.

questions.q: Among ethane, chloroethane, ethanol and dimethyl ether, which has the highest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, giving it a boiling point of about 78 degrees C, higher than the others.

questions.q: Bromoethane reacts with aqueous KOH to give mainly
questions.explanation: Aqueous KOH brings about nucleophilic substitution (OH- replaces Br-), whereas alcoholic KOH causes elimination.

questions.q: Bromoethane heated with alcoholic KOH gives
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HBr in an elimination (dehydrohalogenation) reaction to give an alkene.

questions.q: Bromomethane is treated with sodium metal in dry ether (Wurtz reaction). The main organic product is
questions.explanation: 2CH3Br + 2Na gives CH3-CH3 + 2NaBr, joining two alkyl groups.

questions.q: Propene undergoes hydroboration followed by oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. The main product is
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov alcohol, so the OH goes to the terminal carbon.

questions.q: What happens when phenol is treated with sodium hydroxide? What does this show?
questions.answer: Phenol reacts with NaOH to form sodium phenoxide and water, C6H5OH + NaOH gives C6H5ONa + H2O. This shows that phenol is acidic, unlike alcohols which do not react with aqueous alkali.
keyPoints: Alcohols do not react with NaOH
questions.explanation: The phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance.

questions.q: Why is p-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol?
questions.answer: The nitro group is strongly electron-withdrawing through its -I and -M effects. It delocalises and stabilises the negative charge on the p-nitrophenoxide ion, so the ion forms more easily and the compound is a stronger acid.
keyPoints: Stabilises the phenoxide ion by delocalisation
More stable conjugate base means stronger acid
questions.explanation: Electron-releasing groups such as methyl have the opposite effect.

questions.q: Proteins are polymers of
questions.explanation: Amino acids are linked by peptide bonds to make proteins.

questions.q: When an aldehyde is warmed with Fehling's solution, the precipitate formed is
questions.explanation: The copper(II) complex is reduced to red-brown copper(I) oxide.

questions.q: Reduction of propanone with sodium borohydride gives
questions.explanation: Ketones are reduced to secondary alcohols.

questions.q: Aniline reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate of
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group strongly activates the ortho and para positions, so all three are brominated.

questions.q: Benzenediazonium chloride on treatment with cuprous chloride gives
questions.explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction, in which the diazonium group is replaced by Cl, giving chlorobenzene with loss of nitrogen.

questions.q: One strand of DNA has the base sequence 5'-ATGC-3'. The complementary strand reads
questions.explanation: A pairs with T and G pairs with C, and the strands are antiparallel, so the partner reads 3'-TACG-5'.

questions.q: What are essential amino acids? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Essential amino acids are those that the human body cannot synthesise and must obtain from the diet. Examples are valine, leucine, lysine and isoleucine.
keyPoints: Cannot be synthesised by the body
Examples such as valine, leucine or lysine
questions.explanation: Non-essential amino acids, such as glycine and alanine, can be made in the body.

questions.q: Why are carboxylic acids much more acidic than phenols?
questions.answer: On losing a proton, a carboxylate ion has its negative charge shared equally between two oxygen atoms by resonance, which stabilises it well. The phenoxide ion delocalises the charge onto carbon atoms of the ring, which is less effective, so carboxylic acids ionise more.
keyPoints: Carboxylate charge shared between two electronegative oxygens
Phenoxide charge sits partly on carbon
More stable anion gives stronger acid
questions.explanation: Typical pKa values are about 4.8 for ethanoic acid and 10 for phenol.

questions.q: The testes lie outside the abdominal cavity in the scrotum because
options: spermatogenesis needs a temperature slightly lower than body temperature
they cannot fit inside the body
questions.explanation: The scrotum keeps the testes about 2 to 3 degrees C below body temperature, which is required for sperm production.

questions.q: The cell formed by the fusion of a sperm and an ovum is the
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg is the zygote, which divides repeatedly to form the embryo.

questions.q: In the human female, FSH from the pituitary mainly
options: stimulates the growth of ovarian follicles
questions.explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone promotes the development of follicles and the secretion of oestrogen.

questions.q: Which of the following is a barrier method of contraception?
questions.explanation: Condoms physically block sperm from reaching the ovum and also reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections.

questions.q: The acrosome at the head of a sperm contains enzymes that
options: help the sperm penetrate the layers surrounding the ovum
determine the sex of the child
carry the nutrients to the zygote
questions.explanation: Acrosomal enzymes such as hyaluronidase digest the corona radiata and zona pellucida so that the sperm can reach the ovum.

questions.q: A woman who breastfeeds her baby intensively often does not ovulate for some months. This is because
options: milk contains hormones that block ovulation directly
high prolactin and the suckling reflex suppress the hormones that trigger ovulation
the ovaries are removed during lactation
questions.explanation: The suckling reflex raises prolactin and suppresses the release of gonadotropins, so ovulation and menstruation are delayed, though this is not a reliable contraceptive.

questions.q: Trace the path of sperm from the testis to the outside of the body.
questions.answer: Sperms pass from the seminiferous tubules to the rete testis, then through the vasa efferentia to the epididymis, then the vas deferens, the ejaculatory duct and finally through the urethra to the outside.
keyPoints: Seminiferous tubules, rete testis, vasa efferentia
questions.explanation: Secretions of the seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands add to form semen.

questions.q: Describe the role of hormones in childbirth (parturition).
questions.answer: Signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta cause mild uterine contractions, called the foetal ejection reflex. This stimulates release of oxytocin from the mother's pituitary, which causes stronger contractions, and the cycle repeats until the baby is delivered.
keyPoints: Oxytocin released from the mother's pituitary
questions.explanation: The placenta also releases relaxin, which helps soften the pelvic ligaments.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The process of copying DNA before cell division is called
questions.explanation: DNA replication produces two identical DNA molecules from one.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: An individual with the genotype Tt for a trait is called
questions.explanation: Heterozygous individuals carry two different alleles of the gene.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: A woman with blood group O marries a man with blood group AB. Which blood group can their child have?
questions.explanation: The mother can give only i; the father gives IA or IB, so the child is IAi (group A) or IBi (group B); AB and O are not possible.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: The Meselson-Stahl experiment showed that DNA replication is
questions.explanation: Each new DNA molecule has one old parental strand and one newly made strand.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: In the lac operon of E. coli, when lactose is absent the repressor protein
options: binds to the operator and blocks transcription of the structural genes
binds to lactose and activates the genes
binds to the promoter and starts transcription
questions.explanation: Without an inducer the repressor sits on the operator and RNA polymerase cannot transcribe the lac genes.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Miller's experiment on the origin of life used an electric spark in a flask containing
options: methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour
questions.explanation: With these gases at about 800 degrees C, amino acids were formed, supporting the idea of chemical evolution.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Explain what is meant by the semi-conservative nature of DNA replication.
questions.answer: During replication the two strands of the parent DNA separate and each acts as a template for a new complementary strand. Every daughter DNA molecule therefore consists of one original strand and one newly synthesised strand.
keyPoints: Daughter DNA has one old and one new strand
questions.explanation: Meselson and Stahl showed this using heavy nitrogen (15N) labelling.

questions.topic: Genetics, Molecular Basis of Inheritance and Evolution
questions.q: Why are X-linked recessive disorders such as haemophilia more common in males than in females?
questions.answer: A male has only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele on it is expressed. A female has two X chromosomes and shows the disease only if both carry the recessive allele; a carrier female with one normal allele is usually unaffected.
keyPoints: One recessive allele is enough in males
questions.explanation: Affected males inherit the allele from carrier mothers.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms is a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Fungi break down dead organic matter and return nutrients to the soil.

questions.q: A plasmid is
options: a circular extra-chromosomal DNA molecule in bacteria
a protein in the cell wall
questions.explanation: Plasmids replicate independently of the chromosome and are used as vectors in gene cloning.

questions.q: Net primary productivity is equal to
options: gross primary productivity minus respiratory losses
the energy in the sunlight falling on the area
questions.explanation: NPP = GPP - R is the organic matter available to consumers.

questions.q: Which process removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Green plants take up CO2 and fix it into carbohydrates during photosynthesis.

questions.q: Top carnivores are far fewer in number than herbivores in an ecosystem mainly because
options: they are larger and eat plants
energy is lost at each trophic level, so less is available at the top
questions.explanation: Only about 10 per cent of the energy passes to the next level, which limits the number of top consumers.

questions.q: In agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
options: cathode (negative electrode), the larger fragments faster
anode (positive electrode), the smaller fragments faster
anode (positive electrode), the larger fragments faster
cathode (negative electrode), the smaller fragments faster
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged because of its phosphate groups, so it moves toward the anode, and smaller fragments move faster through the gel.

questions.q: What is a genetically modified organism (GMO)? Mention two benefits of GM crops.
questions.answer: A GMO is a plant, animal or microbe whose genes have been altered using recombinant DNA technology. Benefits of GM crops include resistance to pests (Bt cotton), tolerance to stress, longer shelf life and enhanced nutrition such as in golden rice.
keyPoints: Organism with altered genes through rDNA technology
questions.explanation: GM crops can also reduce the use of chemical pesticides.

questions.q: Explain how Bt toxin kills insect larvae without harming the Bt crop plant.
questions.answer: The plant produces the toxin as an inactive protoxin. In the alkaline gut of the insect larva the protoxin is converted into its active form, which binds to the midgut cells, creates pores and causes them to swell and burst, killing the larva.
keyPoints: Protoxin is inactive in the plant
Pores in midgut cells cause lysis
questions.explanation: The plant cells and human gut lack the conditions or receptors that activate the toxin.
